objective: Give LLM/OCR, provider token refresh, and cloud backup one typed owner for outbound HTTP URL parsing, allowlist matching, and SSRF-relevant host facts without centralizing their domain policies.

production_adapters: LLM and vision OCR provider base URL validation
OAuth-style provider token endpoint refresh validation
cloud backup WebDAV, OSS, S3, COS, and Azure endpoint validation
shared_facts: strict trimmed HTTP/HTTPS URL parsing with control-character, backslash, credential, and missing-host rejection
normalized same-origin and exact-or-origin allowlist matching
localhost, metadata, loopback, private, link-local, unspecified, multicast, and public host classification
adapter_owned_policy: provider default host lists and same-origin decisions
existing environment variable names and reads
which local HTTP scopes are allowed
domain-specific public error messages and response mapping
rejected_expansion: a network client or request executor in core
a trait, service, port, policy DSL, UnitOfWork, cache, or second config source
a universal provider policy that would erase domain differences
additional matching action or BillCreateDraft abstraction without a second real adapter

retained_exceptions: LLM/OCR and token refresh may use allowlisted localhost or loopback plain HTTP
backup sync may use allowlisted localhost, loopback, or private plain HTTP
private and loopback HTTPS still require the existing domain allowlist/default decision

evidence: credentials, control characters, backslashes, non-HTTP schemes, and missing hosts fail before adapter policy or network use
metadata, known metadata IP, link-local, unspecified, and multicast classes fail before allowlist acceptance in all three adapters
the core owner reads no environment variables, resolves no DNS, creates no client, logs no secret, and sends no request
provider token refresh reuses the validated Url and the negative async contract proves rejection before request dispatch

dual_axis_review.reviewed_diff: working tree on codex/c7r-outbound-url-facts, including the zero-behavior Rust 1.98 Clippy compatibility follow-up for XLS parsing and import-config authentication, and excluding the unrelated user-owned .claude/settings.local.json change

standards.evidence: The shared value object is process-local and pure; environment reads, provider domains, HTTP exceptions, public errors, and request execution remain adapter-owned. The CI follow-up retains the existing fixed-width parser and direct Axum Response behavior behind narrow version-compatible lint scopes and changes only equivalent reserved-sector membership and owned test-string construction. No trait, service, port, policy DSL, cache, database, API, schema, money, or user-scope expansion was introduced.

spec.evidence: LLM and vision OCR, provider token refresh, and backup sync all consume OutboundHttpUrl; the three duplicate origin helpers are absent; never-allowlisted classes and retained localhost, loopback, and private policy differences are pinned by behavior and ownership contracts.

test_gaps: request-time DNS resolution and DNS rebinding are not exercised because the accepted slice owns lexical URL facts only
redirect destinations and proxy routing retain their existing client behavior and are not claimed as C7r coverage

verification.delivery_evidence: Pending exact-head Gitea PR, Actions, squash merge, and source-branch deletion.

residual_risks: URL host classification is lexical and does not resolve DNS, so DNS rebinding protection remains the responsibility of request-time network policy.
Adapters intentionally retain distinct allowlist variables and HTTP exceptions; future adapters must not bypass the typed parse/classification boundary.
Explicit proxy behavior and redirect targets are outside this pure URL-facts slice; current provider clients retain their existing redirect policy.

environment_hygiene.provider_strategy: No live LLM, OCR, OAuth token, backup upload, or other paid external request is executed.
environment_hygiene.secrets: Tests use synthetic URLs and never print or persist allowlist credentials, tokens, request bodies, or headers.
